messages:
Anya: quick spike summary — I ran a small canary for a "shadow read" fallback when prefix handoff/demote races cause a miss. overall idea: concurrently hit the old owner for a sampled subset, compare, and swap to fallback if mismatch > threshold. results below.
Kyle: nice. metric-wise what did you measure? read p95/p99 impact? :eyes:
Anya: p95 +12ms, p99 +45ms for sampled requests (we only shadow 5% of traffic). mismatch rate observed ~0.06% for the canary tenant. read-after-write regressions were the main source.
Rachel: can we avoid extra tail by doing async verify + probabilistic repair? i.e. return primary result immediately, but if shadow disagrees mark for fast rehydrate. keeps latency low.
Anya: that's the current approach in the spike: immediate response, verification off-path. if mismatch we trigger a fast prefix rehydrate RPC and emit a retry token. pseudo-config used:
```
shadow_read:
  enabled: true
  sample_rate: 0.05
  verify_mode: async_sampling   # async vs sync vs blocking
  fallback_mismatch_threshold: 0.001  # fraction
  rehydrate_window_ms: 100         # aggressive window for fast repair
```
Tom: concern: what about correctness for long-running writes where the owner has a lag? async repair could make stale data more visible briefly. also rehydrate RPCs could cause thundering if many mismatches.
Kyle: suggested mitigation: circuit-breaker on rehydrate per-prefix and exponential backoff per-tenant. plus a global rehydrate budget. metrics: track rehydrate_rps, rehydrate_fail_rate, shadow_mismatch_rate.
Rachel: also add consistency-tagging on write path (small seq id). shadow comparison compares seq ids first before full payload to reduce cost. if seq matches, skip payload diff.
Anya: yep we added a cheap header check in the spike: `X-prefix-seq` to short-circuit diffs. reduced payload compare CPU by ~70%.
Tom: rollout plan? we should stage on low-impact tenants + opt-in flag for Dedicated. also need runbook: how to abort if rehydrate floods.
Kyle: propose phases: 1) internal-only spikes (5% tenants) 2) canary 5% traffic on non-critical clusters 3) opt-in alpha for dedicated customers 4) gradual ramp with metrics gating. gating: shadow_mismatch_rate < 0.5% and rehydrate_rps < 0.2% of normal read rps.
Anya: volunteers for runbook and dashboard? I can take dashboard + alerting (shadow_mismatch_rate, rehydrate_rps, avg rehydrate latency). need someone for the runbook and canary automation.
Rachel: I can draft runbook steps: abort, throttle, revert config, and manual prefix quarantine. will post WIP tomorrow.
Tom: I'll add the circuit-breaker + per-prefix cooldown patch.
Anya: thanks! last note: canary-bot reported a small spike in rehydrate RPCs during test — see logs — but it was within budget. @canary-bot any deployment metadata? :robot_face:
canary-bot: Canary rollout started: shadow-read v0.1 -> 5% traffic on cluster-a at 2025-04-03T14:22Z. health checks: ok. rolling back on any alert > 5m sustained for mismatch or rehydrate_rps.
Anya: perfect. I'll post a short RFC follow-up with the final config and gating thresholds later today. :thumbsup:
